title: Namibia: the Kalahari to Etosha
best_months: May to October for the full route: dry, cooler days, and game gathers at Etosha's waterholes as the bush dries out. April and early November are good shoulder months. November to February is very hot at Sossusvlei and the north gets its rains from roughly January to March, when game disperses away from the waterholes. Indicative only; sources in practicalities/sources.
summary: A loop of about two weeks that begins on the red sand of the Kalahari, reaches the dunes at Sossusvlei before the day visitors, and runs up the coast and through Damaraland to Etosha. Most of the driving is on gravel, and most of the nights are at places with a guide who will take you out on foot or by vehicle: a rhino track on the Grootberg plateau, a morning in the dunes behind Swakopmund, leopard collars at Okonjima.
vehicle: A high-clearance 4x4 or 4x4 SUV (a double-cab pickup or similar), not a camper. Most of the route is gravel. A 4x4 matters for: the C14/C19 gravel through the Kuiseb and Gaub passes and the Zaris pass (Wikipedia notes the C19 section is often in poor condition and advises against it without 4x4); the 5 km of deep sand from the 2x4 car park to Sossusvlei/Deadvlei, if self-drive access is still permitted at all (see practicalities); and the Grootberg plateau ascent, which the lodge allows only for 'skilled 4x4 drivers' (others leave the vehicle at the guarded gate and are driven up). Two spare wheels and a compressor/pressure gauge are recommended by several sources; confirm what the rental includes.

days.notes: Collect the vehicle, buy a local SIM, draw Namibian dollars. A first night in or near Windhoek avoids a long first drive after an international flight and any risk of arriving after dark. Windhoek stay not yet chosen; see NOTES.md (decision for Dom).

days.road_surface: Tar on the B1 south; the last stretch to the ranch is off the D1268 (surface unverified). Kalahari Anib is reachable by sedan on the C20.
days.notes: An easy first driving day on tar. Arrive for a sundowner drive on the dunes. Fuel up in Mariental before tomorrow.

days.road_surface: Tar from Mariental to Maltahöhe (about 90 km); gravel from Maltahöhe to Sesriem, including the Zaris pass, which is steep and narrow in places.
days.notes: Refuel at Maltahöhe: one route guide says there is no fuel after it until Sossus Oasis, and the NWR pump at Sesriem has been unreliable through 2026. Start early to arrive well before the Sesriem gate closes at sunset.

days.distance_km: about 60–65 each way, Sesriem to the 2x4 car park (unverified), plus 5 km of sand
days.road_surface: Tar inside the park to the 2x4 car park, then 5 km of deep sand to Sossusvlei and Deadvlei.
days.notes: Go in with the lodge's guided sunrise excursion rather than driving the sand yourself. Guests inside the park gate can enter before sunrise; day visitors cannot. Afternoon: Sesriem Canyon on foot, or rest through the heat. Self-drive access beyond the 2x4 car park is unclear in 2026; see practicalities.

days.road_surface: Gravel from Sesriem to Solitaire (about 83 km) and on the C14 through the Gaub and Kuiseb passes to Walvis Bay; tar on the B2 from Walvis Bay to Swakopmund.
days.notes: Stop at Solitaire for fuel, tyre checks and the bakery. No fuel between Solitaire and Walvis Bay. The Kuiseb pass has sharp turns; take it slowly.

Morning: a guided Living Desert tour into the dune belt between Swakopmund and Walvis Bay (08:00 to about 12:30, cash only). Afternoon free. A good day to have the vehicle checked and tyres looked at before Damaraland.

days.distance_km: about 325–450 depending on routing (sources differ; the Spitzkoppe detour adds distance)
days.road_surface: Tar on the B2 inland; gravel to Spitzkoppe and from Uis to Twyfelfontein. Exact surfaces of each segment unverified.
days.notes: The longest day. Leave Swakopmund early, walk at Spitzkoppe mid-morning, and take lunch and fuel at Uis. If the morning slips, drop Spitzkoppe rather than drive into the evening.

days.distance_km: unverified (lodge source gives about 90 minutes' drive)
days.road_surface: Gravel (C39/C40). The final ascent to the plateau is a steep 4x4 track; most guests leave the vehicle at the guarded gate and are driven up.
days.notes: Morning at the Twyfelfontein rock engravings before the heat. Short drive, arrive for lunch and the view off the plateau edge.

Rhino tracking on foot with the conservancy's trackers (an early start, three-quarters of a day; minimum two guests; not for under-16s; sightings not guaranteed). Alternatively, desert-adapted elephant tracking.

days.distance_km: about 330–380 via Kamanjab and Outjo to Andersson Gate (estimate; unverified)
days.road_surface: Gravel on the C40 for the 97 km to Kamanjab; tar beyond. Inside Etosha, Andersson Gate to Okaukuejo is 17 km.
days.notes: Refuel at Kamanjab or Outjo: NWR pumps inside Etosha have been unreliable through 2026. Be inside the camp before the gate closes at sunset. Evening at the floodlit waterhole. An alternative entry via Galton Gate (about 70 km of tar from Kamanjab) is possible but means a long gravel crossing of western Etosha; check with the road book.

days.road_surface: Gravel park roads; 60 km/h limit inside the park.
days.notes: Drive yourself between waterholes, or join an NWR guided morning, afternoon or night drive. The night drive is the only way to be out in the park after dark.

days.distance_km: about 140–210 inside the park (sources conflict) plus a short drive out through Von Lindequist Gate
days.drive_hours: A full day of game viewing; about 2 hours without stops
days.road_surface: Gravel park road, partly under upgrade to a sealed road in 2026 with detours reported between Okaukuejo and Halali.
days.notes: Cross the park slowly via Halali. Allow for detours on the main road. Leave the park through Von Lindequist Gate before sunset (Onguma is outside the park) or be inside Namutoni camp by then.
Fischer's Pan and the eastern waterholes by yourself, or a guided Etosha drive from the lodge. Onguma also has walks and hides on its own reserve.

days.road_surface: Tar via Tsumeb, Otavi and Otjiwarongo on the B1; then about 24–26 km of gravel from the B1 turn-off to the camps.
days.notes: Easy tar day. Arrive for an afternoon activity. The turn-off is just after the 'Otjiwarongo 50km' sign if coming from the south, or after 'Okahandja 130km' from the north.
Leopard tracking by radio telemetry, a visit to the AfriCat research centre, or (extra cost) rhino or pangolin tracking. Sightings are not guaranteed.

days.road_surface: Gravel to the B1, then tar
days.notes: Return the vehicle. Allow time for the rental inspection; tyre and windscreen damage from gravel is common.

stays.name: Bagatelle Kalahari Game Ranch
stays.area: Kalahari, between Hardap and Stampriet, about 45 km from Mariental
stays.access_notes: About 260 km (2.5 hours) south of Windhoek. Address given as off the D1268 near Mariental. Surface of the final stretch unverified. The dune chalets involve a walk through deep sand.
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, half board (dinner, bed and breakfast). ZAR 3,800, converted at 16.38 ZAR/NAD per USD. Source is a search-result snippet from safari.com; the page itself did not render the figure. Treat as weak; confirm with the lodge.
stays.sets_it_apart: Dune chalets raised on stilts on a red Kalahari dune, looking over the inter-dune plain.
guided_activities: San-guided cultural walk (a demonstration, per ExpertAfrica)
stays.ownership: Owner-run private ranch (owners not named in sources); formerly a sheep and cattle farm.
stays.why_we_list_it: The first night out of Windhoek, and the first gravel. Ask for a dune chalet: they stand on stilts on the crest of a red dune, and the evening drive ends on another one with a drink while the light goes off the grass.
stays.cautions: ExpertAfrica's reviewers had reservations about the captive cheetah experience and do not generally recommend it; we would not promote it. Guiding on drives described as variable. Walking guides do not carry rifles (low wildlife densities). Rate source is weak.

stays.name: Kalahari Anib Lodge
stays.area: Gondwana Kalahari Park, about 30 km north-east of Mariental
stays.access_notes: Reachable by sedan along the C20 (per Gondwana).
stays.rate_year: Shown on Gondwana's site, November 2026 (season year not stated on page)
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, bed and breakfast, Standard Twin. N$2,829 at 16.38 NAD/USD.
stays.sets_it_apart: A private Kalahari reserve with a San-guided 'Bushmen Wisdom' walk and guided dune walks, at a lower price than Bagatelle.
guided_activities: Morning/afternoon nature drive with dune sundowner (N$1,000 pp)
Bushmen Wisdom Experience with a local guide (N$935 pp)
stays.why_we_list_it: The plainer, cheaper way into the Kalahari, and an easy one: tar most of the way, a sundowner on a dune, and a morning walk with a San guide before the drive to Sesriem.
stays.cautions: A larger group-run lodge; less individual than Bagatelle. Rate season not stated on the page.

stays.name: Sossus Dune Lodge
stays.area: Sesriem, inside the Namib-Naukluft National Park gate
stays.access_notes: Inside the park's outer gate at Sesriem. Guests use the inner gate, which opens before the main gate (05:00–19:00 Sep–Apr, 05:45–19:00 May–Aug per Viatu's October 2026 guide; versus 06:00/06:45–18:00 for the main gate). Distance from the gate is reported inconsistently; coordinates are from NWR's map link.
stays.rate_year: Nov 2026–Jun 2027 (high season Jul–Oct 2027: N$7,000, about US$427)
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, dinner, bed and breakfast, Dune Chalet. N$4,030 at 16.38 NAD/USD. Park fees extra.
stays.sets_it_apart: The only lodge inside the gate, so guests are in the dunes before sunrise and can stay after sunset.
guided_activities: Guided drive in the park or to the vlei (N$750 pp)
Guided excursion to Elim Dune (N$440 pp)
Guided walk to Sesriem Canyon (N$440 pp)
stays.why_we_list_it: Its position is the point. You leave through the inner gate in the dark and reach Deadvlei while the pan is still in shadow and the car park is empty, which no lodge outside the park can offer.
stays.cautions: NWR service is uneven by reputation (not sourced here; Dom to judge). NWR online booking was unavailable when checked; bookings by email. Fuel at Sesriem unreliable in 2026.

stays.name: Kulala Desert Lodge
stays.access_notes: Entrance 17 km south of Sesriem on the D826 (signposted from the C19); reachable by sedan per Travel Butlers. Guided early-morning drives to the dunes leave through the reserve's private gate on the Tsauchab River.
stays.rate_year: 1 Nov–19 Dec 2026 (US$679 Jun–Oct 2026 and 20 Dec 2026–5 Jan 2027; NAD 6,855 ≈ US$418 for 6 Jan–31 Mar 2026)
stays.rate_basis: Per person per night, fully inclusive: all meals, twice-daily scheduled activities, park fees, laundry, local drinks.
stays.sets_it_apart: A private gate into the park on the Tsauchab River, and rooftop sleep-outs on each room.
guided_activities: Guided early-morning drive to Sossusvlei and Deadvlei via the private gate
Hot-air balloon (extra cost; not 25 Dec–1 Jan or mid-Jan to mid-Feb)
stays.ownership: Part of the Wilderness collection (operator); reserve ownership not confirmed in sources.
stays.why_we_list_it: The upgrade at Sossusvlei: the guides take you through a private gate on the riverbed to the dunes, and you can sleep on the roof of your room under the desert sky. Everything is included, which takes some of the arithmetic out of a long trip.
stays.cautions: Top of our range or above it in peak season. Private-gate access for self-drivers is via the lodge's guided drives only.

stays.name: The Delight Swakopmund
stays.access_notes: Corner of Theo Ben Gurirab Ave and Nathaniel Maxuilili St, a short walk from the Mole. Secure parking listed, but the page says 'at main lodge'; confirm.
stays.rate_year: Shown on Gondwana's site, November 2026 (season year not stated)
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, bed and breakfast, Twin Room. N$2,106 at 16.38 NAD/USD.
stays.sets_it_apart: A well-run town hotel with a good breakfast, walking distance from the seafront; the right base for a day off the road.
guided_activities: No in-house activities; staff book external tours (Living Desert tour, boat trips)
stays.why_we_list_it: Two nights in a town after a week of gravel: a hot shower, a walk along the Mole, and a morning in the dunes with someone who knows where the geckos sleep. It is a hotel, not a lodge, and priced like one.
stays.cautions: Does not meet STRATEGY §4 criterion 3 by itself (no in-house guiding); listed as an on-the-road stop with the Living Desert tour as the guided element. Confirm parking.

stays.name: Strand Hotel Swakopmund
stays.access_notes: On the Mole, about four hours west of Windhoek on tar.
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, bed and breakfast, 'from' NAD 4,397 at 16.38 NAD/USD. Undated; confirm.
stays.sets_it_apart: Built out on the Mole with the Atlantic on three sides; four restaurants including a seafood and oyster bar and a micro-brewery.
guided_activities: No in-house guiding found; external tours bookable
stays.why_we_list_it: For those who would rather wake to the sea than the street. A big hotel, 125 rooms, but the position on the Mole is the best in town.
stays.cautions: Large hotel (125 rooms); fails the 'small, characterful' instinct and §4 criterion 3 on its own. Rate undated. Ownership unverified.

stays.name: Camp Kipwe
stays.access_notes: On the D2612 in the Twyfelfontein area; gravel. Whether 2WD is sufficient is unverified (we are recommending 4x4 for the route regardless).
stays.rate_year: 2026: N$5,070 Jan–Mar and Dec; N$6,700 (≈US$409) Apr–Nov
stays.rate_basis: Per person per night, bungalow, half board (dinner, bed and breakfast); activities extra. Converted at 16.38 NAD/USD.
stays.sets_it_apart: Nine round stone-and-thatch bungalows built into a granite kopje, with open-air bathrooms, a short drive from the Twyfelfontein engravings.
guided_activities: Elephant nature drive in search of desert-adapted elephants (N$1,140 pp in 2024 rack; 2026 price unverified)
Twyfelfontein engravings, Organ Pipes and Burnt Mountain excursion (about N$1,110 pp, 2027 rack)
Guided nature walks in the Twyfelfontein Conservancy
stays.why_we_list_it: The bungalows are tucked between granite boulders, and the bathrooms are open to the sky. From here the rock engravings at Twyfelfontein are a short drive in the cool of the morning, and the guides go out after desert elephants in the dry riverbeds.
stays.cautions: Ownership and conservancy relationship not confirmed. Elephant drive price for 2026 unverified.

stays.name: Damaraland Camp
stays.area: Huab River valley, Torra Conservancy, Damaraland
stays.access_notes: Leave the vehicle at a farmstead by the C39 and transfer to camp (recommended for 2WD), or drive in with a 4x4 only (ExpertAfrica). One source says no self-drive is permitted within the conservancy; confirm with Wilderness.
stays.rate_year: 2026: NAD 9,131 (6 Jan–31 Mar); US$697 (Apr–May, 1 Nov–19 Dec); US$990 (Jun–Oct and 20 Dec 2026–5 Jan 2027)
stays.rate_basis: Per person per night, fully inclusive: meals, twice-daily activities, park fees, laundry, local drinks. NAD figure converted at 16.38.
stays.sets_it_apart: A long-running partnership with the Torra Conservancy; the camp is part-owned by the community and run almost entirely by community members.
guided_activities: Desert-adapted elephant tracking along the Huab
stays.ownership: Wilderness with the Torra Conservancy; part-owned by local people (ExpertAfrica; Chalo Africa says 'owned and largely run by the local communities').
stays.why_we_list_it: The higher-priced choice in Damaraland, and the one with the longest record of the community owning a share of the place. You leave the car and are driven into the Huab valley, where the guides track desert elephants along the dry riverbed.
stays.cautions: Above our US$150–600 band from April to December; peak is about US$990 pppn. Self-drive access rules conflict between sources.

stays.name: Grootberg Lodge
stays.area: Etendeka plateau, ≠Khoadi-//Hôas Conservancy, on the C40 between Kamanjab and Palmwag
stays.access_notes: 97 km west of Kamanjab and 25 km east of Palmwag on the C40 gravel road. Only skilled 4x4 drivers may drive the steep ascent with sheer drops; everyone else leaves the vehicle under 24-hour security at the base and is driven up by the lodge.
stays.rate_year: Shown on lodge booking site, November 2026
stays.rate_basis: 'From NAD 4,520 per night' for a double/twin room. The page does not say whether this is per room or per person, nor the meal basis. If per room, about US$138 pp sharing; if per person, about US$276. Confirm.
stays.sets_it_apart: Wholly owned by the ≠Khoadi-//Hôas Conservancy, on the edge of the Etendeka plateau, with rhino tracking on foot in the conservancy.
guided_activities: Black rhino tracking on foot and by open vehicle (three-quarters of a day; minimum 2; no under-16s)
stays.ownership: 100% owned by the ≠Khoadi-//Hôas Conservancy (opened 2005); managed under contract by Journeys Namibia (GSTC report). One source describes the arrangement as a joint venture.
stays.why_we_list_it: The lodge sits on the lip of the plateau with the Klip River valley falling away below the deck, and the conservancy that owns it sends its trackers out with you after black rhino. It is one of the clearest cases in Namibia of a community owning the place you sleep in.
stays.cautions: Rate basis unclear. Rhino tracking price not published (a 2023 rack sheet listed 2,185 per person, currency not shown). Rhino sightings not guaranteed. The ascent is not for inexperienced 4x4 drivers.

stays.name: Palmwag Lodge
stays.area: Palmwag Concession, Kunene (a few km north of the junction at Palmwag)
stays.access_notes: A few kilometres north of the C43 junction near Palmwag; self-drive supported, fuel station on site (07:00–19:00). Road surface not stated by Gondwana; gravel in practice per the Grootberg directions (unverified for this exact stretch). Note: Gondwana's page says C43/C49 junction; to be checked against the road book.
stays.rate_year: Shown on Gondwana's site, November 2026 (transfer rates on the same page valid 1 Nov 2026–31 Oct 2027)
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, bed and breakfast, Standard Twin. N$3,000 at 16.38 NAD/USD.
stays.sets_it_apart: The gateway to the 582,000-hectare Palmwag Concession, with half-day rhino tracking and an under-canvas sleep-out.
guided_activities: Half-day rhino tracking on foot (N$4,375 pp ≈ US$267; minimum 2; no under-12s)
stays.ownership: Gondwana Collection. Concession arrangements with local conservancies not confirmed in sources.
stays.why_we_list_it: The alternative to Grootberg for travellers who would rather not leave the car at the bottom of a mountain. You drive straight in, fill the tank on site, and go out after rhino in the concession the next morning.
stays.cautions: Less individual than Grootberg; Gondwana-group property. Rhino tracking is a significant extra cost.

stays.name: Okaukuejo
stays.area: Etosha National Park, 17 km from the southern (Andersson) gate
stays.access_notes: 17 km inside the southern entrance on park roads. Filling station and shop on site, but NWR park pumps were unreliable through 2026: arrive with enough fuel.
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, bed and breakfast, Double Room. N$1,900 at 16.38 NAD/USD. Waterhole Chalet N$2,380 (≈US$145) in the same period. Park fees extra.
stays.sets_it_apart: A floodlit waterhole inside the camp fence, watched day and night; black rhino, lion and elephant come to drink after dark.
stays.why_we_list_it: Not a lodge in our usual sense, and we list it anyway. Book a waterhole chalet, eat early, and spend the evening on the bench at the floodlit waterhole, where rhino come down to drink in the dark a few metres from the wall.
stays.cautions: Below our price band and a large state-run rest camp; service and upkeep are uneven by reputation (not sourced). Ask for a waterhole chalet. Fuel unreliable.

stays.name: Etosha Safari Lodge
stays.area: C38, about 10 km south of Andersson Gate
stays.access_notes: About 10 km south of Andersson Gate on the paved C38; suits 2WD; secure parking.
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, bed and breakfast. N$3,721 at 16.38 NAD/USD.
stays.sets_it_apart: Outside the park but ten minutes from the gate, with guided Etosha drives that leave before sunrise.
guided_activities: Guided half-day Etosha drive (N$1,090 pp, park fees extra)
stays.why_we_list_it: For those who want a lodge rather than a rest camp at the Okaukuejo end of the park. It is ten minutes from the gate, and the guided drives go in before sunrise.
stays.cautions: Outside the park: you must be out of Etosha by sunset each evening. Larger group lodge.

stays.name: Onguma Bush Camp
stays.area: Onguma Nature Reserve, beside Etosha's eastern (Von Lindequist) gate
stays.access_notes: On a 35,970-hectare private reserve described as one of the closest bases to Etosha's eastern gate. Exact distance and road surface not stated on the page.
stays.rate_year: 2027 season (1 Nov 2026–31 Oct 2027), Rondavel; Deluxe Room N$4,450 (≈US$272)
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, dinner, bed and breakfast (basis from Onguma's official 2025 rack sheet; Chalo Africa labels the same figures 'all inclusive', which looks wrong). N$3,060 at 16.38 NAD/USD, plus a conservation levy (N$275 pppn in 2025).
stays.sets_it_apart: A waterhole in front of the dining deck, a treetop hide and a water-level hide, and guided walks on the private reserve.
guided_activities: Etosha excursions through Von Lindequist Gate
Game drives on the Onguma reserve
stays.ownership: Onguma Safari Camps (private reserve); owners not named in sources.
stays.why_we_list_it: The eastern end of Etosha is quieter, and Onguma gives you a private reserve to walk on as well as the park to drive in. The waterhole is in front of the dining deck, so dinner tends to be interrupted.
stays.cautions: Rate basis to confirm. Three deluxe rooms are in an unfenced area, not recommended for young children.

stays.name: Namutoni
stays.access_notes: Inside the park near the eastern (Von Lindequist) gate. NWR fuel unreliable through 2026.
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, bed and breakfast, Double Room. N$1,840 at 16.38 NAD/USD. Park fees extra.
stays.sets_it_apart: Sleeping inside the park beside the floodlit King Nehale waterhole, which means first light on the eastern waterholes without a gate queue.
stays.why_we_list_it: The inexpensive choice in eastern Etosha, and the only one inside the fence. You are on the road to Fischer's Pan as the gate opens.
stays.cautions: Below our band; state-run rest camp. Service uneven by reputation (not sourced).

stays.name: Okonjima Plains Camp
stays.area: Okonjima Nature Reserve (about 22,000 ha), between Otjiwarongo and Okahandja
stays.access_notes: Gravel turn-off from the B1 (just after the 'Otjiwarongo 50km' sign from the south); 10 km of gravel to the reserve gate and 14–16 km more to the camps. About 2.5 hours from Windhoek on tar, 3 hours from the international airport. Check road conditions in the rains.
stays.rate_year: 2026: N$4,830 low season (1 Jan–30 Jun), N$5,320 (≈US$325) high season (1 Jul–31 Dec)
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, dinner, bed and breakfast/brunch, Classic Room; includes NTB levy and VAT. Park levy N$350 pppn extra. Activities extra (2026 rack lists activities from N$880 to N$2,900 pp; individual activity mapping not legible in the extracted sheet). Converted at 16.38 NAD/USD.
stays.sets_it_apart: Home of the AfriCat Foundation's research; leopard tracking by radio telemetry on a reserve where many of the leopards are collared.
stays.ownership: Okonjima (family-run per general reputation; not confirmed in sources), with the AfriCat Foundation based on the reserve.
stays.why_we_list_it: The last stop before the airport, and a good one to end on. The guides go out with an antenna after collared leopards, and the AfriCat team explain what the collars are for. Plains Camp is the plainer, better-value way to stay.
stays.cautions: Activities are charged separately and add up quickly. Leopard sightings are not guaranteed. Cheetah tracking no longer appears on the current activity list; don't promise it.

stays.name: Okonjima Luxury Bush Camp
stays.access_notes: Same access as Plains Camp: 24–26 km of gravel from the B1.
stays.rate_year: 2026: N$10,140 low season (1 Jan–30 Jun), N$11,160 (≈US$681) high season
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, DBB chalet including drinks (excl. premium/imported), laundry, NTB levy, VAT. Fully inclusive option N$13,900/15,300 with 2 activities per day (excl. rhino and pangolin tracking). Park levy N$350 pppn extra. Converted at 16.38 NAD/USD.
stays.sets_it_apart: Chalets set apart in the bush with their own waterhole views; the more private way to stay at Okonjima.
stays.why_we_list_it: The quieter end of Okonjima, for a last night that is about the bush rather than the drive home.
stays.cautions: Above our band (about US$619–681 pppn on DBB, more fully inclusive). Not clearly better value than Plains Camp View Rooms (N$7,000–7,700 ≈ US$427–470); Dom to decide.

stays.name: Solitaire
stays.area: Junction of the C14 and C19, between Sesriem and Walvis Bay
stays.access_notes: About 83 km of gravel from Sesriem and about 230 km of gravel from Walvis Bay. Petrol station, tyre repairs, a general dealer, a small restaurant and a bakery; two lodges (Solitaire Country Lodge, Solitaire Guest Farm).
stays.rate_basis: Lunch and fuel stop; no overnight proposed.
stays.sets_it_apart: The only fuel and tyre repair for a long way in either direction, and a bakery known for its apple strudel.
stays.ownership: Mixed; the bakery was founded by Moose McGregor (died 2012). One review says Cafe van der Lee has taken over the bakery; current operator unverified.
stays.why_we_list_it: A filling station, a tyre workshop and a bakery at a crossroads in the gravel, with old car wrecks in the sand out front. Fill the tank, have the tyres checked, and buy a slice of strudel for the Kuiseb.
stays.cautions: Current bakery operator unverified; don't name it in copy until checked.

stays.name: Spitzkoppe
stays.access_notes: Gravel access off the B2. Day visitors pay an entry fee at the community rest camp reception (current amount unverified; sources range widely). Guides wait at Small Bushman's Paradise; rock-art walks are paid by tip or a small fee (sources conflict).
stays.rate_basis: Day visit; entry fee to community rest camp (unverified).
stays.sets_it_apart: Granite peaks rising out of the gravel plain, with San rock paintings at Bushman's Paradise shown by community guides.
guided_activities: Community-guided rock-art walk to Bushman's Paradise (about 2 hours)
stays.ownership: Spitzkoppe Community Rest Camp; campsites managed by the Spitzkoppe Group on contract from the community (namibweb).
stays.why_we_list_it: A mid-morning walk on the way north. The community guides take you up into the granite to the paintings at Bushman's Paradise, and you are back on the road to Uis by lunch.
stays.cautions: Not proposing Spitzkoppen Lodge as an overnight: ownership is unclear and its construction was reportedly disputed by the traditional authority and conservancy (article no longer online; see NOTES). Entry fees unverified.

stays.name: Uis
stays.area: Former tin-mining town, south-east of the Brandberg
stays.access_notes: Nearest town to the Brandberg (about 30 km) for fuel and basic supplies. Cactus and CoffeeTea Garden (Daureb Isib) serves coffee, cake and light food.
stays.sets_it_apart: The last proper fuel before Twyfelfontein, and a cactus nursery that serves coffee.
stays.why_we_list_it: Fuel, and coffee in a cactus garden, in an old mining town on the way into Damaraland.

borders: None on the core route; it stays inside Namibia.

For the 'Windhoek to the Falls' extension, a rental vehicle needs a cross-border letter from the rental company (about NAD 500 per one source; some companies charge far more, and some bar Zambia entirely) plus road-user charges at each border. Confirm in writing with the rental company. Sources: https://roadgenius.com/cars/rental/namibia/ , https://www.sixt.com/rental-information/na/car/ , https://namibiawetland.com/access-zambezi/
practicalities.fuel: Fill up in every town. Namibian filling stations are attended (tip the attendant). NWR pumps inside Etosha (Okaukuejo, Halali, Namutoni) and at Sesriem were unreliable through at least April 2026: refuel at Maltahöhe or Solitaire for Sossusvlei, and at Outjo, Kamanjab or Tsumeb for Etosha, and enter Etosha with enough to finish the crossing. No fuel between Solitaire and Walvis Bay. Fuel at Palmwag Lodge (07:00–19:00). Sources: https://umhambi.blogspot.com/2026/02/nwr-fuel-shortage-update-february-2026.html , https://namibweb.com/solitaire-namibia.htm , https://gondwana-collection.com/accommodation/palmwag-lodge
practicalities.cash_and_payments: The Namibian dollar is pegged one-to-one to the South African rand, and the rand is legal tender in Namibia. Card acceptance at filling stations is inconsistent and card machines fail; carry cash for fuel, tips and the Living Desert tour (cash only). Rates in this file converted at 16.38 NAD per USD (currency.me.uk reference rate, 27 October 2026; not a live rate). Sources: https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/selected-issues-papers/2026/english/sipea2026060.pdf.md , https://wild-wings-safaris.com/frequently-asked-questions/what-do-i-need-to-know-about-driving-in-namibia , https://www.currency.me.uk/convert/usd/zar?amount=1
practicalities.park_fees: From 1 April 2026, international adults pay N$280 per day at premium parks (Etosha, Namib-Naukluft including Sossusvlei, Waterberg); children 9–16 N$140; under 8 free; vehicles with 2–10 seats N$50 per day. Paid at the gate or rest camp in 24-hour blocks. Some guides still show older figures (for example Viatu's N$80); the newer figure is supported by the Observer24 report and the gazette. Sossusvlei shuttle from the 2x4 car park: about N$250–260 return per adult. Sources: https://safarifind.com/blog/namibia-national-park-fees-availability-2026 , https://www.observer24.com.na/?p=43973 , https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2026/8877.pdf , https://atta.travel/resource/sossusvlei-and-deadvlei-tighten-access.html
practicalities.gate_times: Etosha: gates open at sunrise and close at sunset; times change weekly and are posted at each gate and camp. You must be out of the park or inside an NWR camp by sunset; it is the driver's responsibility to know the time. Speed limit inside Etosha 60 km/h. Sesriem (Sossusvlei): main gate 06:00–18:00 Sep–Apr and 06:45–18:00 May–Aug; inner gate for guests of Sossus Dune Lodge and Sesriem camp 05:00–19:00 / 05:45–19:00 (Viatu, updated October 2026; other sources give different times, so confirm on arrival). No driving after dark anywhere on the route: wildlife and livestock on unlit roads, and many rental agreements restrict or prohibit it (check the contract wording). Plan every day to arrive at least an hour before sunset. Sources: https://nwrnamibia.com/etosha-gate-opening-times.htm , https://anywhereweroam.com/self-drive-etosha-safari/ , https://www.viatu.com/en/blog/namibia/a-complete-guide-to-sossusvlei , https://info-namibia.com/info/faq
practicalities.gravel_driving: Most of this route is gravel. ExpertAfrica recommends an absolute maximum of 80 km/h on any gravel road, lower where the surface is poor; most visitor accidents involve going too fast on gravel and losing control, and on loose gravel that means rollovers. Brake early, corner gently, avoid sudden steering. Stated legal limits on gravel vary between sources (80 or 100 km/h); drive to the road, not the sign. Headlights on at all times. Slow right down for oncoming dust clouds and blind rises. Punctures are common: check both spares before leaving Windhoek, carry a compressor and gauge, and have tyres checked at each town. Lowering pressure 10–20% on gravel is optional; reinflate on tar, because soft tyres on tar overheat and can blow out. The C19 Zaris pass and C14 Kuiseb pass have steep, tight sections. Sources: https://expertafrica.com/namibia/info/self-drive-driving-tips-and-techniques , https://www.namibian.com.na/why-tyre-pressure-matters-off-road/ , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C19_road_(Namibia) , https://travelbutlers.com/property/kulala-desert-lodge/
practicalities.rental_and_cross_border: Rent a 4x4 (double-cab or SUV) with two spare wheels; confirm tyre and windscreen cover, which gravel damages most. Driving is on the left. A US or UK licence in English with a photo is generally accepted; carry an International Driving Permit as a backup (sources differ on when it is required). Sossusvlei: from 15 December 2025, ATTA reported all private vehicles restricted to the 2x4 car park with access beyond only by the concession shuttle or authorised guided vehicles; Viatu (updated October 2026) says MEFT confirmed in May 2026 that 4x4 self-drivers may continue to Deadvlei. Until resolved, we plan for the lodge's guided excursion or the shuttle. Cross-border: see borders. Do not name a rental company in copy (STRATEGY D-03). Sources: https://atta.travel/resource/sossusvlei-and-deadvlei-tighten-access.html , https://www.viatu.com/en/blog/namibia/a-complete-guide-to-sossusvlei , https://tyremap.com/as-tourist/driving-in-namibia-as-united-states-tourist/

variants: Shorter (12 nights): one night in the Kalahari is dropped by driving Windhoek to Sesriem direct, one night in Swakopmund instead of two, and one night at each end of Etosha. Loses the slack days; not recommended for first-time gravel drivers.
Waterberg instead of Okonjima: the Waterberg Plateau Park is a premium park near Otjiwarongo and works as the last night before Windhoek. Not researched for this file.

Windhoek to the Falls: from eastern Etosha continue north-east to the Zambezi Region and Victoria Falls instead of returning to Windhoek, joining R3. One-way rental and cross-border fees apply. Adds roughly 5–7 nights (estimate).
More Damaraland: add a night at Palmwag or a second at Twyfelfontein for desert elephant tracking; takes the pressure off the long day 7.
